_about: DNN field reports, live interviews, weather desk. See ../COPY.md.

tavern.text: {reporter} here, live from {place}, where the mood is best described as 'one more round'. Back to you in, they tell me, one more round.
I'm standing in the {place_kind}, and I can confirm: the mugs are full, the bard is loud, and nobody here has watched the news in weeks.
{reporter} live from {place}. The barrels are running dry and the crowd is getting restless. I am being told to wrap this up quickly and leave.
The scene here at the {place_kind} is tense. Two dwarves are arguing over whether the last song was about a battle or a cheese. Both are crying.
{reporter} reporting. Behind me, a dwarf has been telling the same story about a carp for three hours. The carp gets bigger every time.
I'm live in {place}, where a cat has claimed the warmest seat by the hearth. Locals tell me challenging the cat is not done here.
The ale is flowing here in the {place_kind}, and so, frankly, are the confessions. I've learned things tonight, {anchor}. Things I cannot unhear.
Reporting from {place}. A dancer just knocked over three mugs and a performer. The performer is fine. The mugs, I am sorry to say, did not make it.
{reporter} at the {place_kind}. I asked the patrons for a comment on current events and was handed a drink instead. I'm calling that a no comment.
Live from {place}, where the visiting poet has been reciting for so long that two dwarves have aged into the elderly bracket. Truly moving work.

temple.text: {reporter} here, live from {place}. It is very quiet, {anchor}, so I will be whispering this entire report. The gods appreciate it. Probably.
I'm standing in the {place_kind}, where a dwarf has been praying for a full day. Sources say it's either deep devotion or they fell asleep on their knees.
Live from {place}. Worshippers tell me they come here for peace, reflection, and to get away from the noise of the tavern. Mostly the last one.
The {place_kind} is packed today, {anchor}. Nothing brings dwarves closer to the divine like a long week of hauling stone.
{reporter} reporting. A priest here just asked me to stop filming the altar. I'm told the altar is shy. I'll respect that and film this wall instead.
Live from {place}, where dwarves have gathered to remember the departed. A sombre scene. Even the cats are sitting still, which is unheard of.
Here in the {place_kind}, faith runs deep. I asked one worshipper what they pray for. They said 'better ale' and then looked very embarrassed.
{reporter} live in the {place_kind}. Someone has left an offering of a single roasted turnip. Theologians are already divided on its meaning.
Live from {place}. A choir is performing, though I'm told only half of them know the words. The other half are humming with great conviction.
This is {reporter} at the {place_kind}, where a dwarf in a strange mood just walked in, stared at the ceiling, and left. Experts say that's normal. Experts lie.

library.text: {reporter} live from {place}, where a scholar has been reading the same page since spring. They say the plot is really picking up.
I'm in the {place_kind}. Silence is strictly enforced, so I've been asked to report this entirely in a polite murmur. Murmur murmur. Back to you.
Live from {place}. Researchers here are hard at work on a treatise titled, and I'm quoting, 'Rocks: A Second Look'. It is eleven volumes.
The {place_kind} is open, the scrolls are stacked, and two scholars are in a fierce debate about whether elves can read. Neither has met an elf.
{reporter} here. A dwarf just checked out a book on carp safety. Given recent events at the lake, {anchor}, that is a wise choice.
Live in the {place_kind}, where a cat is asleep on the only copy of an important history. Nobody has the courage to move it. History will wait.
{reporter} reporting from {place}. The librarian informs me the most borrowed book this month is 'Ale Through the Ages'. Second place: a sequel.
Here in the {place_kind}, knowledge is power. I asked a scholar what they're studying. They said 'everything'. Then they asked me to leave.
{reporter} live. This shelf behind me holds every recorded complaint the nobles have ever made. It is load-bearing, {anchor}.
Live from the {place_kind}. A young scribe is copying a manuscript by candlelight. The candle is the most dangerous thing in this room. Tense stuff.

hospital.text: {reporter} live from {place}. The doctors are busy, the beds are full, and someone keeps asking for ale as medicine. The doctors are considering it.
I'm at the {place_kind}, where a dwarf with a broken leg is insisting he's 'fine, just resting'. He has been resting for forty days.
Live in the {place_kind}. The bone doctor tells me business is steady. When I asked what 'steady' means, she just pointed at the stairs.
{reporter} here. A patient behind me has been waiting for a crutch since last season. The crutch is reportedly still a tree somewhere.
Live from {place}, where the soap supply is, and I quote the staff, 'a matter we don't discuss on camera'. We move on.
{reporter} reporting from the {place_kind}. Morale is surprisingly high. One patient told me the food here is the best in the fort. It's the same food.
Here at {place}, a surgeon is washing her hands for the third time. I'm told it's either good practice or nerves. She did not answer me.
Live in the {place_kind}. A soldier just came in with a goblin arrow in his helmet and asked if he could keep it. Doctors said yes. Very brave, very silly.
{reporter} at the {place_kind}. It's been quiet here lately, {anchor}. The staff have taken up knitting. One bed now has a sweater.
This is {reporter} at the {place_kind}, where the thread stockpile is low and the patience is lower. Back to you before I'm asked to hold something.

guildhall.text: {reporter} live from {place}, where the guild is meeting to discuss a pressing issue: who gets the good chair. Talks have stalled.
I'm in the {place_kind}. The members here take their craft very seriously. One just told me a hammer is 'a lifestyle'. I nodded.
Live from the {place_kind}, where guild dues are being collected. Several members are suddenly very interested in a crack in the ceiling.
{reporter} reporting. The guild has issued a formal statement on the quality of recent work. The statement is a single disapproving grunt.
Here in {place}, the guildmaster is giving a speech on tradition. It started at breakfast. It is now well past dinner. He's on part two.
{reporter} live at the {place_kind}. Members are displaying their finest work. One brought a mug. Just a mug. They're very proud of it.
Live from {place}. I've been told outsiders are not allowed past the second bench, so this is as close as DNN can get. It's a nice bench.
The {place_kind} is buzzing tonight, {anchor}. A rumour is going around that someone outside the guild made a masterwork. Outrage is building.
{reporter} here. The guild just voted unanimously to hold another vote. Democracy is alive and very, very slow in {fort}.
Live in the {place_kind}, where an apprentice has been asked to fetch 'the left-handed anvil'. We at DNN will not spoil the joke for him.

dining.text: {reporter} live from {place}, where the lunch rush is in full swing. I've already been elbowed twice. A third elbow is approaching.
I'm in the {place_kind}. The table behind me has been arguing for an hour about whether a roast is better with or without a cave spider in it.
Live in the {place_kind}. Portions are small today, {anchor}. One dwarf just ate a single mushroom very slowly, with great dignity.
{reporter} here. There's so much food in the {place_kind} that a dwarf just fell asleep face-first in a stew. He looks content.
Live from {place}. The cook tells me tonight's special is the same as last night's special. When asked what it is, she said 'special'.
{reporter} reporting from the {place_kind}. A noble has requested a private table. There are no private tables. He is now eating standing up, alone, furious.
Here in the {place_kind}, a cat has stolen a fish right off a plate. The owner of the plate has decided this is now the cat's fish. Wise.
{reporter} at {place}. The tables are crowded, the chairs are mismatched, and someone is eating raw plump helmets out of protest. Against what, unclear.
Live in the {place_kind}. A dwarf just stood on a table to make a toast. The toast was to the table. Everyone cheered. A moving moment.
This is {reporter} in {place}, where the dishes are piling up. Nobody does the dishes, {anchor}. We don't even have dishes. That's the mystery.

barracks.text: {reporter} live from {place}. The militia is training hard today. I have been asked to stand further back. Then further. I'm now in a hallway.
I'm in the {place_kind}, where the squad is sparring. One recruit just dodged so well he dodged right out of the room. Still looking for him.
Live from the {place_kind}. The captain tells me morale is high and the armour is mostly the right size. Mostly.
{reporter} here. Soldiers are sleeping in shifts. The current shift is sleeping. The next shift is also, as far as I can tell, sleeping.
Live in {place}. Without a siege to worry about, the squad has invented a new drill: standing very still and looking intimidating. It works on me.
{reporter} reporting from the {place_kind}. A soldier is polishing an axe and humming. It's a lovely tune. I'm going to leave now.
Here at the {place_kind}, the militia commander gave me one rule: don't touch the weapon rack. I touched it. I'm being escorted out shortly.
Live from {place}, where a recruit has asked if the training spears are 'the pointy end or the other end'. The sergeant has gone for a walk.
{reporter} live. The squad behind me is wrestling. Rules are simple: there are none. Score is unclear. Everyone is losing, mostly to the floor.
This is {reporter} at the {place_kind}. Training is going well, though one soldier keeps saluting the cat. The cat has not saluted back.

pasture.text: {reporter} live from the {place_kind}. Behind me, a yak is staring at the camera. It has been staring for some time. I don't like it, {anchor}.
I'm standing in {place}, where the animals are grazing and the smell is, let's say, a big story of its own.
Live in the {place_kind}. A goat just ate part of our equipment. The goat has been asked for comment. The goat has eaten that too.
{reporter} here, ankle-deep in the {place_kind}. I've been told the grass is fresh. I've also been told not to look down. Both are true.
Live from {place}. The cats have wandered out here too, {anchor}. They're not grazing. They're supervising. The cows look nervous.
{reporter} reporting. A dwarf is trying to herd turkeys. The turkeys are herding him. It's an even contest and I'm calling it for the turkeys.
Here in the {place_kind}, a newborn calf is taking its first steps. Locals have already named it. They've also already discussed it as stew. Tough crowd.
Live in {place}. The animal trainer tells me the war dogs are well behaved. One is currently eating my notes. Well behaved, though.
{reporter} live from the {place_kind}. It's peaceful out here. Just grass, sky, and a single alpaca that has decided I am its enemy.
This is {reporter} in the {place_kind}, where a pig has escaped and is now running a victory lap. Nobody is chasing it. It respects that.

depot.text: {reporter} live from the {place_kind}, where everyone is waiting for the caravan. Some have waited so long they've started a small settlement.
I'm at the trade depot. The broker is practising her haggling face. It's terrifying, {anchor}. I would sell her anything.
Live from the {place_kind}. Haulers are lining up crafts for trade. Someone has stacked forty stone mugs and labelled them 'heirlooms'.
{reporter} here. A rumour has spread that elves are coming to trade. Three dwarves have already hidden the wooden furniture. Out of spite.
Live at the depot, where the broker just offered a merchant a crate of rock crafts for one barrel of ale. The merchant is weeping. Hard bargain.
{reporter} reporting from the {place_kind}. It's empty right now, {anchor}. Just me, the wind, and a dwarf who swears she heard wagons.
Here at the depot, the guards are on alert. One asked me if I was a merchant. I said no. He seemed disappointed. I am disappointed too.
Live from the {place_kind}. A noble has come down personally to inspect the goods. He's inspecting them very closely. With his pockets.
{reporter} live. The haulers are moving bins at top speed. When asked why, one said 'the broker looked at me'. That's all you need, really.
This is {reporter} at the {place_kind}, where the last caravan left behind a single sock. It's now being treated as a historical artefact.

workshop.text: {reporter} live from {place}. Hammers ringing, sparks flying, and a craftsdwarf who has told me to stop asking questions three times.
I'm at the {place_kind}. The work orders are stacked high. When I asked the crafter how many there are, she said 'yes'.
Live in the {place_kind}, where a dwarf is in a strange mood and demanding materials. Nobody knows what she wants. She just keeps pointing at my hat.
{reporter} here. A mason is carving a statue that's either a hero, a dragon, or a really big potato. Too early to tell. Exciting times.
Live from {place}. The workshop is a mess, {anchor}. Tools everywhere, shavings everywhere. The crafter says it's 'organised by feel'.
{reporter} reporting from the {place_kind}. Behind me, a carpenter has just made his ninetieth bed. He shows no signs of stopping. Pray for him.
Here in the {place_kind}, I asked what they're making. 'Something good,' I was told. Then the dwarf made a mug. It's a good mug, though.
Live in {place}. Someone has requested a masterwork. The crafter laughed for a full minute, then got to work. That's dwarven confidence.
{reporter} live at the {place_kind}. A cat is asleep on the workbench. The work is not happening. The cat is happening.
This is {reporter} at the {place_kind}. The craftsdwarf here hasn't slept in two days but has made some truly beautiful buckets. Priorities.

farm.text: {reporter} live from the {place_kind}. Plump helmets as far as the eye can see, which underground is about four tiles. Still. Impressive.
I'm in the fields, where the farmers are planting. One tells me the secret is to talk to the crops. He's been shouting at them since dawn.
Live from {place}. The harvest is coming in strong, {anchor}. Or at least the farmer is. He's carrying more than I thought possible.
{reporter} here. The {place_kind} smells of fresh soil and fertiliser. Mostly fertiliser. Let's move this along.
Live in the {place_kind}. With food running short, every plant here is being watched closely. One farmer is guarding a single sprout.
{reporter} reporting. The farmers have a strict policy: no cats in the fields. There are six cats in the fields. The policy is being reviewed.
Here in the {place_kind}, a dwarf is harvesting sweet pods. He's eating about one in four. Officially, that's quality control.
Live from {place}. Spring planting is underway, and the farmers are optimistic. Then again, they're always optimistic. It's the spores.
{reporter} live at the {place_kind}. A farmer just told me she's growing 'the best pig tails in the mountain'. I have no reason to doubt her.
This is {reporter} in the {place_kind}. The rows are neat, the soil is rich, and someone has planted a mushroom in the shape of a noble. Bold.

dig.text: {reporter} live from the mining face. The dust is thick, the picks are swinging, and I can't see a thing, {anchor}. Great report so far.
I'm deep in the tunnels, where the miners have just struck what they're calling 'very nice rock'. Experts confirm: it is rock.
Live from the dig. A miner tells me they're going deeper. When I asked how deep, he said 'until something stops us'. Comforting.
{reporter} here, at the edge of the new tunnel. The miners have asked me not to breathe so loud. I'm told it echoes. It does.
Live in the mines, where a dwarf just found a gem and shouted so loud a second dwarf dropped his pick on his own foot. A mixed day.
{reporter} reporting from the dig site. Somewhere below us is magma. The miners say they know exactly where. They do not say this confidently.
Here at the mining face, the rule is simple: don't dig straight down. A dwarf behind me is digging straight down. We'll keep you posted.
Live from the tunnels. A miner has been carving the same corridor for weeks. He says it's for 'a project'. The project is a longer corridor.
{reporter} live underground. The miners have broken into a cavern. Something in there made a sound, {anchor}. We are now leaving very professionally.
This is {reporter} at the dig. The picks are sharp, the ore is shiny, and one miner has taken to naming every boulder. This one is 'Old Lumpy'.

entrance.text: {reporter} live at the main entrance, where the guards keep watch for goblins, elves, and anyone who still owes the tavern money.
I'm standing at the gates of {fort}. It's the only place in the fort you can see the sky. Several dwarves are refusing to look at it.
Live from the entrance. A migrant wave is expected soon, {anchor}. The welcoming committee is one dwarf and a sign that says 'mind the traps'.
{reporter} here. The drawbridge is down, the guards are up, and a wild badger has just walked in like it pays rent here.
Live at the gates. It's quiet out here, {anchor}. With only {pop} of us, every face that walks through this door is big news.
{reporter} reporting from the entrance. A dwarf just stepped outside, looked at the sun, and came right back in. Can't blame him.
Here at the front door of {fort}, the cage traps are armed. One is occupied. By a squirrel. The squirrel is under investigation.
Live at the gate, where the guards tell me the most dangerous thing they've seen this week is a hauler with a wheelbarrow and no brakes.
{reporter} live outside. Fresh air, open sky, and absolutely no ale. Honestly, {anchor}, I don't know how the surface folk live like this.
This is {reporter} at the entrance of {fort}. We're watching the horizon for travellers. So far: a cloud. A threatening cloud, but a cloud.

machine.text: {reporter} live from the pump station, where a dwarf has been working the pump all day. He says it's for the fort. He looks very tired.
I'm standing beside the windmill. It's turning, {anchor}. That is the whole story. It's a good windmill. Back to you.
Live at the mist generator, where dwarves come to feel the spray and be happy. I'm feeling it now. I'm very damp and somewhat happy.
{reporter} here. The gears are turning, the axles are spinning, and an engineer is explaining it all to me. I've understood none of it.
Live from the machinery room. A lever behind me is labelled 'do not pull'. Someone has crossed that out and written 'probably fine'.
{reporter} reporting from the pump stack. Water is going up. Or possibly down. The engineer says it's going 'where it should'. Great.
Here by the waterwheel, a dwarf is staring at the paddles, entranced. He's been here since the last season. He calls it 'meditation'.
Live in the machine room, where the hum of power is constant. So is the noise. I'm shouting, {anchor}. I'VE BEEN SHOUTING THE WHOLE TIME.
{reporter} live. The engineers here have built a contraption nobody fully understands. It works. Nobody touches it. That's engineering.
This is {reporter} beside the pumps. If this report gets cut off, it's because someone pulled the wrong lever. Again. Back to y—

generic.text: {reporter} live from somewhere in {fort}. Our crew isn't entirely sure where we are, {anchor}, but the walls are very well smoothed.
I'm standing in a hallway in {fort}. Not much going on here. A dwarf walked by a minute ago. That was the news. Back to you.
Live from the heart of {fort}. Dwarves are hauling, crafting, and occasionally stopping to stare at a wall. It's a typical day.
{reporter} here. I've been told to find a story, {anchor}. I found a sock. I'm going to stay with the sock for now.
Live in {fort}, where {citizen} just walked past the camera, waved, and tripped. We wish them well. We also have it on tape.
{reporter} reporting. It's {season} in {fort}, and the corridors are busy. Everyone is going somewhere. Nobody will tell me where.
Here in {fort}, the mood is cautiously optimistic. That's dwarf for 'nothing is on fire right now'.
Live from {fort}. I've asked a passer-by for comment. He said 'move'. I moved. Good journalism is about listening.
{reporter} live. Behind me you can see {citizen} and {citizen2} having what appears to be a very intense discussion about a bucket.
This is {reporter}, somewhere in {fort}. I'm told this spot will be an important room someday. Today it's a spot. Back to you, {anchor}.

interview_q.text: {guest}, thanks for joining DNN. How are you feeling today?
{guest}, what do you think of life in {fort} lately?
{guest}, quick question for our viewers: ale or more ale?
{guest}, how's work going as a {guest_prof}?
I see you're busy with '{guest_job}', {guest}. Tell us about that.
{guest}, what's the biggest problem facing {fort} right now?
{guest}, what do you think of the elves?
{guest}, if you could change one thing about the fort, what would it be?
{guest}, there are reports of too many cats. Your reaction?
{guest}, have you ever had a strange mood?
{guest}, what's your favourite thing about {season}?
{guest}, the nobles have issued new mandates. Thoughts?
{guest}, do you feel safe in {fort}?
{guest}, what would you say to the next wave of migrants?
{guest}, what's the best meal you've had this year?
{guest}, are you worried about goblins?
{guest}, what keeps you going every day?
{guest}, can you describe your bedroom for our viewers?
{guest}, do you have a message for {anchor} back in the studio?
{guest}, what do you make of the latest masterwork?
{guest}, how do you feel about the carp situation?
{guest}, would you ever go to the surface voluntarily?
{guest}, what's your opinion on the current ale supply?
{guest}, the caravan is due soon. What are you hoping for?
{guest}, have you visited the tavern lately?
{guest}, what's the secret to being a good {guest_prof}?
{guest}, some say {fort} is the finest fort in {world}. Agree?
{guest}, what does {civ} mean to you?
{guest}, how do you deal with stress?
{guest}, any thoughts on the state of the hospital?
{guest}, what's the most dangerous thing you've seen this year?
{guest}, do you trust the bookkeeper's numbers?
{guest}, are you a cat dwarf or a dog dwarf?
{guest}, what would you do if you were in charge for a day?
{guest}, there's a rumour about magma in the lower levels. Comment?
{guest}, how would you rate {season} so far?
{guest}, what's one thing viewers don't know about you?
{guest}, are you happy with your job as a {guest_prof}?
{guest}, what's your hope for {year}?
{guest}, do you watch DNN regularly?
{guest}, what's the strangest thing you've hauled?
{guest}, how do you feel about the fort's population of {pop}?
{guest}, what do you think of {citizen}?
{guest}, would you describe yourself as a dwarf of the people?
{guest}, the debate rages: smoothed walls or engraved walls?
{guest}, are things better or worse than last {season}?
{guest}, what would you put on your tomb?
{guest}, any advice for young dwarves just starting out?
{guest}, what's the one thing you'd save in a flood?
{guest}, last question: what's next for you?

happy.text: Honestly? I've never been better. I had a fine drink, I slept in a real bed, and nobody threw anything at me. Perfect day.
Life is good! The ale is cold, the rock is solid, and I saw a very nice cat this morning. What more could a dwarf want?
Oh, I'm delighted. Delighted! I don't know why exactly. Something about today. Maybe it's the smoothed walls.
I just think {fort} is wonderful. Sure, things go wrong. Things always go wrong. But they go wrong beautifully here.
I love it here! I love everyone! Well, most of everyone. I love most of everyone very much.
You know what, I'm grateful. Grateful for the stone, grateful for the mushrooms, grateful for whoever keeps the barrels full.
Can I just say hello to everyone at home? Hello! I'm on DNN! This is the best day of my life. Again.
I'm happy, thank you for asking. Nobody ever asks. I'd like to say more, but I'm happy just standing here.
Great question! I don't know the answer, but I'm in a fantastic mood, so let's say: yes, definitely, all of it.
I'm thrilled. I just admired a fine piece of furniture. It was a chair, but what a chair.
Couldn't be better! I ate a roast, I prayed a bit, and I won an argument. Triple win.
Things are looking up. Not literally, we're underground. But in spirit, very much up.
Everything's great. I've got friends, I've got a mug, and I've got a hat I really like. That's the whole recipe.
I'm content. Deeply content. I think the mist from the generator did something to me, and I'm not complaining.
Wonderful! I'd recommend this fort to anyone. Except elves. But anyone else, absolutely.
With this much ale around? I'd say life is excellent. I'd say it twice, but I've had a few.
It's been so peaceful. No sieges, no beasts. I've had time to just sit. I'm very good at sitting now.
I'm in a great mood. I don't want to jinx it, so I'm going to say nothing else and walk away smiling.

stressed.text: I don't want to talk about it. I want to talk about it so much. But I won't. Is the ale still out there?
Look, I haven't slept, I haven't eaten properly, and someone took my sock. I just need one good thing to happen.
Why is everyone asking me questions? Is something wrong? Did something happen? Nobody tells me anything!
I'm fine. I'm totally fine. I'm just going to go stand in a corner for a while and breathe. That's all.
Honestly, I'm one bad day away from throwing a mug. Not at you. Probably not at you.
Everything is falling apart and I'm the only one who notices. Have you seen the state of the dining hall?
I was rained on, then stepped in something, then a cat looked at me funny. It's been a lot.
I just need someone to fix the hauling. Is that so much to ask? Is it?
I'm not angry, I'm just... very tired. I've been tired since spring. Possibly since birth.
Please don't put me on camera. Oh, it's already on. Great. Wonderful. Hello, everyone.
No comment. Actually, one comment: the nobles are impossible. Okay, that's my comment. Now leave.
I had a dream about carp. I don't want to talk about the dream. I just want to warn everyone.
I haven't seen my friends in weeks. They're all busy. I'm busy. We're all busy being busy.
There's no ale. Do you understand what that means to a dwarf? I'm going to lie down.
I'm hungry. Everyone's hungry. I'm trying not to think about it and you're making me think about it.
It's been a hard time for all of us. I'd rather not talk right now. Thank you.
Everything's fine as long as nothing else goes wrong. And something always goes wrong. So.
I'm one more tantrum away from a tantrum. Mine. Not anyone else's. Just so you know.

neutral.text: It's alright. Could be better, could be worse. That's about all I'll say.
I don't really have an opinion. I'm a dwarf. I dig, I drink, I sleep. That's my opinion.
Hmm. I'll have to think about that. Ask me again in a season.
Well, I suppose it's fine. Everything's mostly fine. Some things are less fine.
No strong feelings either way. I just came here for the ale, honestly.
Couldn't tell you. I've been working. Didn't notice anything.
It's the same as always. Rock, ale, work, bed. And repeat.
I suppose so, yes. Or no. Somewhere in between, really.
Sure. That's one way to look at it. I look at it a different way, but sure.
I'd rather not take sides. I've seen what happens to dwarves who take sides.
Honestly, I just want to get on with my day. But it's nice to be asked.
Not much to say. Things happen. We deal with them. Then more things happen.
It is what it is. I'm told that's very wise. I just say it because it's short.
I'll let the nobles worry about that. They seem to enjoy worrying.
Hard to say. I've only been here a little while. Or a long while. Time is strange underground.
I suppose it depends on the ale. Most things do.
Can I get back to you on that? I'll send a messenger. Probably won't, though.
Fine, fine. Everything's fine. Is this going to be on the news? Okay. Fine.

child.text: I saw a cat! It was big! It was orange! Can I say hi to my mum? Hi Mum!
When I grow up I'm going to be a miner and find a giant gem and fight a dragon. Maybe two dragons.
I don't know. I'm just a kid. Do you have any sweets? Or a rock? I collect rocks.
My favourite thing is the tavern. They play songs! I'm not allowed in after dark though.
Is this the news? Am I on the news? I'm on the news! Everybody, I'm on the news!
I made a toy out of wood! Don't tell the elves. They'd be sad. Or angry. I don't know which.
The grown-ups are always busy. I play with the puppies. The puppies are never busy.
I want to be a soldier! Or a cook! Or a cat. Can dwarves be cats? I think I can.
My dad says I'm too small to haul. I hauled a pebble today. It was a big pebble.
I'm not scared of goblins. I'm a little scared of the dark. And the carp. Mostly the carp.
I found a hole in the wall! I'm not telling anyone where. Except you. It's over there. Don't tell.
I learned a new word today. It's 'mandate'. I don't know what it means, but nobles say it a lot.
Why do grown-ups drink so much ale? Is it nice? They say I'll understand when I'm older.
I'm the fastest kid in the whole fort! Want to see? Okay, wait here. I'll be right back.
I named a turkey. It's a secret name. Nobody's allowed to eat a turkey with a secret name. Ever.
My friend said the magma is lava. I said it's magma. We had a fight. I won.
I don't like baths. Can you put that on the news? No more baths. That's my message.
I asked a noble if he had a real job. He didn't answer. I think that means no.

soldier.text: Sir. Yes, sir. I mean, yes, reporter. I'm ready for anything. Except more questions.
We train every day. Spear, shield, axe. We're ready if the goblins come. Hope they don't. Mostly.
I'm a soldier. I don't have opinions. I have orders. My orders are to stand here. I'm standing.
The squad's in good shape. We've been sparring. Lost two teeth, but they were the spare ones.
If anything comes through those gates, it's dealing with us. Well, the traps first. Then us.
My armour's a bit tight, but the captain says it builds character. I've got a lot of character.
I signed up to protect the fort. Also for the free meals. Mostly to protect the fort.
Can't talk long. Training in a moment. I'm going to hit a dummy. It's had it coming.
Fear? We don't feel fear. We feel... strategic hesitation. Very different.
We stand watch so everyone else can sleep. Somebody has to. Usually it's me. Every night.
The captain says I'm improving. Last week I dropped my spear only twice. Personal best.
Peace is nice. Boring, but nice. I've polished my helmet so many times I can see my soul in it.
I've fought a goblin once. Well, I yelled at one. It left. That counts.
Honour, duty, and a hot meal at the end of a shift. That's all a soldier needs.
I'd tell the viewers to stay calm and stay inside. You're dwarves. You're inside already. Good.
Nothing to report. That's the best thing a soldier can say. Nothing to report.
I've got a squad, a shield, and a mug. I'm prepared for every possible outcome.
We protect {fort}. Anything that wants in has to go through us. Or around us. Please don't go around us.

busy.text: Can we do this later? I'm in the middle of '{guest_job}' and it won't do itself. Believe me, I've waited.
Sorry, sorry, I've got to get back to this. Ask me again when I'm done. I'm never done.
I'm working! Look at me working! I'm going to keep working while you talk. Go on.
No time, no time. I'll give you one word: busy. That's the word. Bye.
You've caught me mid-task. '{guest_job}', if you must know. Very important. Probably.
Talk while I walk. Faster. No, faster. I've got things to carry and you're in the way.
Is this going to take long? Because this job won't finish itself, and I'm the only one doing it.
Look, I'd love to chat, but I promised someone I'd finish this. I don't remember who. Still promised.
Quick answer: yes. Longer answer: also yes. Now please, I've got '{guest_job}' to do.
I'm the only one in this fort who works, you know that? Everyone else is drinking. Put that on the news.
Can't stop. If I stop, I'll sit down. If I sit down, I'll never stand up again. That's how it works.
Hold this. No, don't hold that. Hold this. Okay, give it back. Thanks. Interview over.
My job? '{guest_job}'. It's going fine. It would be going better without a camera in my face.
I'm halfway through something and if I lose my place I'm blaming DNN. On air. Right now.
Busy, busy, busy. Ask the next dwarf. They're not doing anything. Look at them. Not doing anything.
One minute. Maybe two. Okay, now I've wasted one. One minute left. Make it count.
Right now? Right now I'm working. Later I'll drink. Then I'll sleep. Then I'll work again. That's the whole interview.
Sorry, I've got to go. Duty calls. Well, the bookkeeper calls. Same thing really.

rain.text: It's raining on the surface of {fort} today. Down here, it's dry as always. Your forecast: stay inside. You were going to anyway.
Reports of {weather} topside, {anchor}. The few dwarves who went out came back soaked and confused. They've been given towels and ale.
Rain continues to fall above us. Farmers are delighted. Everyone else is underground and frankly doesn't care.
The surface is wet. The depot is wet. The caravan, if it comes, will be wet. Indoors, it's a lovely 'dry with a chance of ale'.
We're getting reports that it's raining. Experts recommend you do absolutely nothing different. As always.
It's a wet one outside. The elves are probably loving it, which is the best argument for staying indoors.
Heavy {weather} at the entrance. The guards have retreated three tiles inward and are calling it 'tactical shelter'.
If you're heading outside today, bring a hood. If you're not heading outside, which is everyone, enjoy your rock.
Rain topside again, {anchor}. The animals in the pasture look miserable. The cats inside look smug. Weather is a zero-sum game.
There's {weather} on the surface. Below the surface, as of this moment, there is still a ceiling. Good news for all of us.
Rain watch: the surface is damp, the moat is fuller, and a dwarf just learned the hard way that mud is slippery.
A rainy {season} for {fort}. Our meteorologist has stepped outside to confirm. She hasn't come back. She's fine. She's just wet.
Autumn rains are here. The trees outside are dropping leaves. The elves are probably sad about it. Good.
Rain on the surface today. For the underground forecast, I'm happy to report: rock, more rock, and a light drizzle from a leaky pipe.

snow.text: Snow on the surface of {fort}. Down here, it's warm, it's cosy, and there's ale. Weather report done.
It's snowing, {anchor}. Our surface correspondent has been asked to stand in it for this report. He says it's cold. Thanks for that.
Winter has arrived topside. Snow covers the entrance. Dwarves are urged to stay inside and appreciate how much rock is above them.
There's {weather} at the gates. The caravan route is a mess. Merchants will be late, cold, and grumpy. So, standard merchants.
Snow continues to fall above. A dwarf child built a snowdwarf. It's frowning. That's very accurate. Well done, kid.
It's a snowy {season}. If you see a cat outside, bring it in. If you see an elf outside, leave it.
Heavy {weather} out there, {anchor}. The pond has frozen. Somewhere under the ice, a carp is planning something.
The surface is white and cold. The tunnels are grey and cosy. We know which one we prefer here at DNN.
Snow report: about a foot of it on the surface. Down here? None. Zero. We live in a mountain. That's the whole point.
Winter weather topside. The haulers moving goods to the depot are bundled up like sacks. Very brave, very lumpy.
Snow has blanketed the outdoors. Our guards report visibility is poor. They can't see goblins. Goblins can't see them. Even trade.
It's snowing above {fort}. Underground, our forecast is: same temperature as yesterday, and the day before, and forever.
A frosty {season} in {world}. If you must go out, wear your thickest socks. If you have socks. Check the stockpile.
The snow keeps coming. The pasture animals are huddled together. Our sources say they've formed a union.

clear.text: Clear skies over {fort} today. The sun is out. Dwarves are advised not to look at it directly. Or at all, really.
It's a clear day topside, {anchor}. Lovely weather for the elves. Terrible weather for anyone who hates the sky.
Not a cloud above {fort}. Great day for a caravan. Even better day to stay inside and drink.
Summer sun is beating down on the surface. Under the mountain, it's a cool, pleasant 'normal'. Same as always.
Clear weather means good visibility at the gates. The guards can see for miles. They've seen trees. They're upset about it.
Sunny skies on the surface. A dwarf who went out to check reported back with one word: 'bright'. Thank you, very helpful.
Beautiful weather outside today. A rare treat. Please enjoy it from the safety of a tunnel.
The sky is clear and blue, {anchor}. I'm told it's very pretty. I wouldn't know. I work in a cave.
A fine clear {season} day. Farmers on the surface are out working. Farmers underground are also working. Same plants, really.
No rain, no snow, no clouds. A perfect day to do exactly what you'd do on any other day: dig.
Clear skies this spring. The trees are blooming outside. Please don't tell the woodcutters. Or do. Your choice.
Clear and calm above. Forecasters say this could last a while. Forecasters also have no idea. It's the sky.
Sunshine on the surface. The cats have gone out to lie in it. Twelve of them. They are not coming back until dinner.
Clear weather topside. A good time to check the drawbridge works. Please don't test it while anyone is standing on it. Again.

other.text: The weather topside today is, frankly, unclear. Something is happening in the sky. We recommend not finding out.
Our weather desk reports conditions on the surface are 'weird'. That's the technical term. We'll update you if it gets weirder.
Fog over the entrance today, {anchor}. The guards can't see a thing. They've been challenging the fog to fight. The fog is winning.
Strange weather above {fort}. The animals are acting odd. The dwarves are acting odd. Business as usual, then.
The weather is doing something today. What exactly, we can't say. Our reporter refused to go out and check. Smart reporter.
Unusual conditions on the surface. If it's raining blood again, please stay inside. If it isn't, please stay inside anyway.
Something is in the clouds, {anchor}. Experts say it's probably nothing. Experts also say 'probably' a lot.
Weather report: it's {season}. Beyond that, we have no idea. We live underground. We don't go outside. Next story.
The sky looks... off today. Cloudy, strange, a funny colour. We're calling it 'atmospheric'. That sounds professional.
Our weather instruments are broken. Our weather instrument is a dwarf holding a stick outside. He's come back in. Stick's fine.
No clear forecast today. Could be rain, could be snow, could be sun. Could be a dragon. Stay indoors just in case.
Windy conditions on the surface. The windmill is spinning like it's never spun before. Engineers are thrilled. Nobody else cares.
It's a grey, gloomy {season} out there. Inside, it's a grey, gloomy {season} too. But with ale. Advantage: inside.
The weather desk is pleased to report that the weather, whatever it is, has absolutely no impact on your life. Back to you, {anchor}.
